content.page_summary: Guidance on anticoagulation and acute management of pulmonary embolism (PE) in pregnancy, use of invasive procedures, role of multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team, and a section on amniotic fluid embolism (AFE).

anticoagulant_recommendations.postpartum_duration: Anticoagulant treatment should be administered for 6 weeks after delivery with a minimum overall treatment duration of 3 months.
anticoagulant_recommendations.breastfeeding: Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and warfarin can be given to breastfeeding mothers; use of non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) is not recommended.
anticoagulant_recommendations.peri-procedural_interval: Allow interval of approximately 8–12 h between prophylactic and next therapeutic dose around catheter removal and similar periprocedural considerations; close collaboration between obstetrician, anaesthesiologist and attending physician is recommended.

acute_management_of_high-risk_PE_in_preg.incidence_note: High-risk, life-threatening PE during pregnancy is rare but potentially devastating.

systematic_review.treatments_used: thrombolysis, surgical thrombectomy, and/or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)
systematic_review.survival_rates: Reported survival rates were 94% after thrombolysis and 86% after surgical thrombectomy (may reflect reporting bias).
systematic_review.major_bleeding_rates: Following thrombolysis, major bleeding occurred in 18% of cases during pregnancy and 58% in the post-partum period.
systematic_review.fetal_death_rates: Foetal deaths occurred in 12% of cases following thrombolysis and 20% following thrombectomy.

acute_management_of_high-risk_PE_in_preg.treatment_guidance: Thrombolytic treatment should not be used peri-partum except in life-threatening PE. Unfractionated heparin (UFH) is typically used in the acute treatment of high-risk PE.
acute_management_of_high-risk_PE_in_preg.vena_cava_filters: Indications similar to non-pregnant patients, but limited experience in pregnancy and potentially increased procedural risk.

multidisciplinary_team_role.section: 9.3.1 Role of a multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team
multidisciplinary_team_role.recommendation: A multidisciplinary team should collaborate to plan ante-, peri- and post-partum care pathways for women with cardiovascular disease including PE. Team members should have expertise in PE management in pregnancy and the post-partum period. Jointly agreed, written care pathways should be available when timelines permit to ensure effective communication.

amniotic_fluid_embolism_AFE.definition: AFE is a rare condition that occurs during pregnancy or shortly after delivery and is a leading cause of direct maternal death in high-income countries.
amniotic_fluid_embolism_AFE.diagnosis: Challenging; primarily a clinical diagnosis of exclusion. Awareness and prompt diagnosis are critical.
amniotic_fluid_embolism_AFE.clinical_features: Unexplained sudden cardiovascular or respiratory deterioration, often accompanied by disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), occurring during pregnancy or after delivery.
amniotic_fluid_embolism_AFE.management_principles: Aggressive life support and prompt diagnosis are of critical importance.

content.references_notes: Statistics and recommendations are supported by cited systematic reviews and referenced evidence (citations indicated in text).
